newsitem.title: USA: Howard Gary seeks reinstatement in Dade Cty deal.
newsitem.headline: Howard Gary seeks reinstatement in Dade Cty deal.

text.p: Howard Gary & Co asked Dade County officials Thursday to reinstate the firm as senior manager of an upcoming $30 million Dade County seaport bond deal.

Dade County removed the firm from the seaport deal on Wednesday, citing a Miami Herald report that company president Howard Gary had secretly recorded a conversation in which he offered Dade County Commissioner James Burke $100,000 to win a spot for Gary's firm on an unrelated Dade County bond deal.
The newspaper said Gary acted in cooperation with federal prosecutors.
Gary protested the ouster in a letter delivered to County Manager Armando Vidal late Thursday.
Reuters obtained a copy of the letter, which noted that Howard Gary & Co had been duly appointed by the county and had "expended considerable ressources and time on this transaction."

The letter also notes that "a California based firm continues to serve as senior managing underwriter for the county's $165 million bond transaction for the arena despite press allegations regarding that firm."

The letter did not identify Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc by name, but that San Francisco firm was selected as senior manager for the arena deal, which is due in December or January if voters approve the bond issue in November.

The California firm was allowed to remain on the deal after The Herald reported that the resignation of its president, Calvin Grigsby, followed questioning by federal prosecutors about a previous Dade County bond deal.

The Herald also reported Thursday that Grigsby was captured on an FBI videotape offering Dade County Commissioner James Burke a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering bond business to Grigsby Brandford & Co.
Federal investigators have refused to comment on any of the reports and neither Grigsby, Gary nor Burke have been charged with any crimes.

County Finance Manager Ed Marquez said Gary had been removed from the seaport deal because the allegations against him "are of such a nature that it would require disclosure on that bond issue. The county's not prepard to do that at this point in time."
Marquez and assistant County Attorney Gerald Heffernan said such a disclosure could prompt and adverse reaction when the deal was priced.

They said timing was also a factor in the decision to remove Gary's from from the seaport deal while allowing Grigsby Brandford to stay on the arena deal. The seaport deal is scheduled to be priced next month, while the county does not plan to begin work on the arena deal until after the November election.
The county will use proceeds from the seaport bond issue to buy a cruise ship terminal built at the Port of Miami by Carnival Corp.

Marquez and Heffernan said both Howard Gary & Co and Grigsby Brandford would remain in the county's underwriting pool and that if they "come out to be in good standing when the smoke clears" they would be allowed to make up for any lost revenues by being appointed more frequently to future bond issues.
Federal prosecutors have declined to comment on the allegations and neither Gary nor Burke has been charged with any wrongdoing.
Burke has resigned as chairman of the county commission's finance committee but remains a commissioner.
Marquez said there has been no price impact on trading of Dade County bonds despite all the allegations.
"I haven't seen any nor would I expect any. All our bond transactions have been done correctly. They're solid investments," Marquez said.
--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013
